verified.name: The Granit Oak (Granitski dab)

location.address: Village of Granit, Bratya Daskalovi municipality, Stara Zagora Province, Bulgaria

verified.access: Free. Stands in the open in Granit village (a signposted natural monument and the region's main tourist draw); protective fencing limits how close visitors get but the tree is fully visible and reachable on foot.
verified.transport: Village of Granit, Bratya Daskalovi municipality, Stara Zagora Province; no rail, reached by road, roughly 30-40 min drive from Stara Zagora or Chirpan
verified.verify_notes: Widely reported as Bulgaria's oldest tree and among the oldest in Europe. Dated in March 1982 by Pressler borer (dendrochronological core), which counted 1637 annual rings, giving a germination date of c. 345 AD; en.wikipedia and bg.wikipedia both cite this ring count as the age method (not a vague estimate, a real dendro reading, though decades old now so age_min/max nudged upward for years elapsed since 1982). Girth 7.45-7.46 m (sources vary by 1cm), diameter 2.38 m, height 23.4 m, historic crown area c. 1017 sq m. Registered in Bulgaria's Century-Old Trees Registry, entry #388 (a national protected-tree register), declared a natural monument in 1967. SEVERE DECLINE, flagged for the writer: its largest branch broke in a 1969 storm and the tree has been dying ever since (low groundwater cited as the unfixable cause); by 2018 only one branch remained alive, propped with a steel structure and old concrete/wire repairs from 1983 that news sources call unsuccessful. A 2024-dated bg.wikipedia revision and a 2024 news search both still describe that one living branch greening each spring, so it is CONFIRMED ALIVE as of 2024, but this is a tree in its final years rather than a healthy specimen; the story should say so honestly rather than presenting the old crown/height/area figures as its current appearance. Coordinates from en.wikipedia (42.254067, 25.136080) and bg.wikipedia (42.254036, 25.136009) agree to within a few metres, tree-level precision.
verified.destination_test: PASS: Bulgaria's most famous named tree, the country's oldest, a signposted natural monument and established regional tourist attraction that people specifically travel to Granit village to see.
